$comment: The credential-FILE vocabulary: the paths that hold a secret. Published so every consumer derives its own file matcher from ONE list instead of keeping a copy that drifts. Read it from Python via agent_sanitizer.secrets (credential_path_matcher and the three *_globs accessors) or from JavaScript via the npm subpath exports `agent-sanitizer/credential-files` (this file) and `agent-sanitizer/credential-files-matcher`. Matching is case-insensitive, so every entry is lower-case. `nameGlobs` match a path's LEAF name (`*` crosses no separator because a leaf holds none). `pathGlobs` match the whole posix path and start `*/`, so the tool directory may sit anywhere. `directories` are exact directory names: any path with one of them as a component counts, so the whole directory is covered. A glob uses only a-z 0-9 _ . - and `*`. A match is a REPORT that a path is credential-shaped, never proof it holds a secret: `*secret*` also names `secrets.py`, `*.key` also names a Keynote file, and `*.pem` also names a public certificate. A consumer that cannot afford that false positive narrows the list on its side.
